hypothesis: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can significantly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of de novo molecular design by integrating external knowledge sources to inform and guide the generative process. RAG systems can retrieve relevant chemical and biological data, which is crucial for navigating the vast chemical space and ensuring the generated molecules meet complex constraints of "drug-likeness" and validity [self-rag:29][denovo-genai-survey:1]. By leveraging retrieval mechanisms, RAG can provide real-time access to up-to-date scientific literature and databases, thereby reducing the time and cost associated with traditional drug discovery methods [denovo-genai-survey:1]. This integration of retrieval with generative models allows for more informed decision-making in molecule and protein design, potentially accelerating the development of novel therapeutics [denovo-genai-survey:1]. Furthermore, the use of RAG in de novo design can facilitate the exploration of unexplored chemical spaces, offering a promising avenue for discovering new drug candidates and advancing synthetic biology [denovo-genai-survey:1].
